bw: Best bedside marker of adequate fluids?
w: Blood pressure stays normal until late in burn shock and is an insensitive guide.
Wedge pressure needs a pulmonary artery catheter and is not used to titrate burn fluids.
p: Titrate burn fluids to urine output (about 0.5 mL/kg/h in adults); the Parkland formula only gives the starting rate.

bw: Back pain worse in morning, better with activity
w: ESR is nonspecific and cannot confirm sacroiliitis.
MRI of the sacroiliac joints is for suspected disease with negative radiographs, not the first test.
p: Ankylosing spondylitis: inflammatory back pain, HLA-B27, and sacroiliitis on radiograph; treat with NSAIDs and TNF inhibitors. Check for uveitis.

bw: Painful arc, pain on internal rotation
w: Adhesive capsulitis limits both active and passive motion globally.
Biceps tendinopathy causes anterior pain with resisted elbow flexion or supination.
p: Impingement and rotator cuff tendinopathy cause pain with abduction between 60 and 120 degrees (painful arc) and a positive Hawkins test.

bw: Visual field loss with macular sparing
w: A right PCA infarct produces a left field defect without alexia, since the language dominant side is spared.
The anterior cerebral artery supplies the medial frontal lobe (leg weakness), not the occipital cortex.
p: Alexia without agraphia follows a left PCA infarct involving the occipital cortex and splenium, with right homonymous hemianopia and possible memory loss.

bw: Drug to prevent MI and stroke?
w: Pentoxifylline may modestly improve walking distance but does not lower cardiovascular events.
Graded exercise improves symptoms but is not a drug that cuts mortality.
p: Peripheral artery disease is a coronary equivalent: antiplatelet therapy (aspirin or clopidogrel), statin, and smoking cessation reduce events.

w: Molluscum gives pearly umbilicated papules, not grouped vesicles on an erythematous base.
Adenovirus causes follicular conjunctivitis without eyelid vesicles.
p: HSV can cause blepharoconjunctivitis and keratitis; treat with antivirals and watch for dendritic corneal ulcers.

x: truncated; key relies on omitted history (mastectomy)
two defensible vaccines (HPV, Tdap, MenACWY) due at age 12

w: Citalopram can reduce cataplexy slightly but does not treat sleepiness first.
Risperidone is an antipsychotic; the hallucinations here are hypnagogic, not psychotic.
p: Narcolepsy: sleep attacks, cataplexy, hypnagogic hallucinations, sleep paralysis; modafinil for sleepiness, sodium oxybate for cataplexy.

w: Peutz-Jeghers has hamartomatous polyps and mucocutaneous pigmentation, not hundreds of adenomas.
Cowden syndrome causes hamartomas, facial trichilemmomas and breast and thyroid cancer.
p: Gardner syndrome is familial adenomatous polyposis (APC) with osteomas, epidermoid cysts, desmoids and CHRPE; colectomy prevents colon cancer.

x: treatment key is a drug combination, ambiguous

w: Digital cervical exam can provoke hemorrhage when a previa is possible.
Coagulation studies help in abruption with DIC but do not locate the placenta.
p: Suspected placenta previa is confirmed by ultrasound (transvaginal is safe and more accurate); never do digital exam until previa is excluded.

bw: Low TSH, high free T4, no goiter
w: Propylthiouracil is for true hyperthyroidism, whereas this transient hCG-mediated state resolves alone.
Methimazole is teratogenic in the first trimester and not needed here.
p: Gestational transient thyrotoxicosis with hyperemesis is treated supportively; antithyroid drugs are reserved for Graves disease.

w: Alport syndrome is a type IV collagen defect with deafness and a family history, not a post-infectious flare.
Immune complex deposition with low C3 follows strep infection after 1 to 3 weeks.
p: IgA nephropathy (Berger) causes hematuria 1-2 days after a respiratory infection (synpharyngitic), with normal complement.

w: Concentric protruding rings are Schatzki rings at the squamocolumnar junction.
A pharyngeal (Zenker) pouch is a posterior outpouching with regurgitation and halitosis.
p: Plummer-Vinson syndrome: iron deficiency anemia, dysphagia from a proximal esophageal web, and glossitis; iron repletion helps.

w: Urinary beta-2 microglobulin marks cadmium tubular injury.
White nail bands (Mees lines) are seen in arsenic poisoning.
p: Lead poisoning: wrist drop, colicky pain, microcytic anemia with basophilic stippling; treat with succimer or EDTA.

w: Repeat screening in 1 year applies when HPV testing is negative.
LEEP is for confirmed high-grade lesions on colposcopy and biopsy.
p: ASCUS with positive HPV goes to colposcopy; if HPV is negative return to routine screening or cotest in 3 years.

w: Amifostine protects against cisplatin renal toxicity and radiation xerostomia.
Mesna prevents cyclophosphamide hemorrhagic cystitis.
p: Leucovorin (folinic acid) bypasses dihydrofolate reductase blockade and rescues cells from methotrexate toxicity.

w: Salmeterol is a long-acting beta agonist and does not cause thrush.
Omalizumab is an anti-IgE injection and does not cause oral candidiasis.
p: Inhaled corticosteroids cause oral candidiasis and dysphonia; rinse the mouth and use a spacer.

w: Sacroiliac inflammation is typical of spondyloarthropathies, not rheumatoid arthritis.
Osteitis deformans (Paget disease) is a focal remodeling disorder of older adults.
p: Systemic inflammation, immobility and glucocorticoids raise osteoporosis risk in rheumatoid arthritis.

w: NF1 mutations cause neurofibromatosis type 1, not MEN2.
VHL deletion causes von Hippel-Lindau disease with hemangioblastomas and renal cell carcinoma.
p: MEN2A: medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma and parathyroid hyperplasia from activating RET mutations; screen relatives and offer prophylactic thyroidectomy.

w: Transabdominal ultrasound is less sensitive for early ectopic pregnancy.
Dilation and curettage would be harmful before confirming the pregnancy is intrauterine.
p: Ectopic pregnancy (prior PID risk): transvaginal ultrasound first; unstable patients go directly to surgery.
